description:
​Hi! I’m Aiman, leading team AstroAura for NASA Space Apps 2026. Focused on "Abandoned but not Forgotten", we're combining physics, logical analysis, and space history to build an interactive platform highlighting iconic rovers and landers left across space.

​Looking for:

• Coders (Web/UI)

• Researchers & Storytellers

• Designers (Graphic/UX)

​Join us to bring space history to life!
summary: Silent Guardians: Forgotten Pioneers of Space is an interactive, non-linear digital storybook that brings humanity’s most iconic dormant and distant spacecraft back into the spotlight. Addressing the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" challenge, it transforms complex orbital telemetry, hardware specifications, and mission milestones into an accessible, self-guided visual archive across the Moon, Mars, and Interstellar Space. By pairing curated space imagery with real-time mission milestones—such as Voyager 1 crossing the 1 light-day threshold from Earth in November 2026—and an interactive comprehension quiz, the project preserves the scientific legacy of the robotic pioneers that paved the way for modern space exploration.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Silent Guardians: Forgotten Pioneers of Space is an interactive, non-linear digital museum that brings humanity’s most iconic dormant and distant spacecraft back into the spotlight. From a central Home Hub, users navigate freely between three visually distinct chapters—The Silver Moon (Apollo 11 Laser Retroreflector & Apollo 15 Lunar Rover), The Red Planet (Opportunity Rover & Ingenuity Mars Helicopter), and Interstellar Space (Voyager 1 Golden Record & Voyager 2 Grand Tour)—using hyperlinked navigation cards and persistent Home buttons. A final Mission Check module features an embedded interactive quiz to test audience retention.

​Benefits & Intended Impact

Space exploration milestones are often buried inside dense technical archives. Our goal is to make legendary robotic missions engaging, intuitive, and memorable for students and general audiences—highlighting how "retired" or distant hardware continues to contribute to science today (such as daily lunar laser ranging and deep-space telemetry).

​Creativity & Key Design Factors

Rather than presenting a static linear slideshow, we designed an interactive storybook experience where each celestial destination has its own custom color palette, typography, and archival atmosphere (Lunar Cyan, Mars Coral, and Voyager Solar Gold). We prioritized clean visual hierarchy, scannable telemetry highlights, and real-time astronomical relevance—including Voyager 1 crossing the historic 1 light-day milestone from Earth (~25.9 billion km) on November 18, 2026.

​Tools & Software Used

  • ​Canva: Used for UI/UX prototyping, custom layout cards, internal slide hyperlinking, and the embedded interactive Mission Check quiz form.
  • ​NASA Open Data & Archival Libraries: Used for verified mission telemetry, flight logs, and spacecraft imagery.
